summary: Adversarial multi-agent code review of the depth-capture build (0087/0088/fn) — find, verify, consolidate; no fixes

confirmed.title: Fresh-open gate and entry-age now measure time-since-ingestion (first_seen), not time-since-Gamma-listing (createdAt) — the flat-open filter becomes near-tautological and mislabels converged books as fresh
confirmed.description: 0086 sourced hoursSinceListing from opening_captures.hours_since_listing, which opening-capture/pure.ts computes as (now - ev.createdAt) using the TRUE Gamma listing time (createdAtGamma), an external anchor. 0088 reconstructs hoursSinceListing = captured_at - me.first_seen (line 71) and createdAtGamma = me.first_seen (line 69), i.e. time since WE first ingested the market. Because depth-capture (depth_capture_targets) can only walk a bucket after discover has ingested it (first_seen set) and it walks every near-dated market within ~5 min, min(captured_at - first_seen) is ~0 for essentially every market it touches, so the fresh gate `min(...) < 1` (line 44) is nearly always true and no longer selects the ~1h-of-listing flat-open cohort the old gate did. The population balloons and, for any market discovered with latency, the panel starts observing an already-converged book and treats it as the flat open, while the maxEntryAgeH=24 cap (measured from first_seen) understates true age and admits later entries. The whole strategy premise is buying at the flat open, and the §9R-E verdict is computed over this population — the repoint silently changes what the panel measures.
confirmed.failureScenario: Gamma lists a °C market at 12:00 (createdAt); discover ingests it at 18:00 (first_seen, 6h late); depth-capture's first depth row is 18:05. hoursSinceListing = 0.08h → passes fresh<1 AND maxEntryAgeH≤24; the panel replays the 6h-converged book as the flat open and logs a 'fresh' entry at an age (0.08h) it never actually had (true 6.08h). Old path: opening-capture enumerated Gamma directly, captured the book at 12:02 with hoursSinceListing≈0.03 from the true createdAt — a genuinely different (real flat-open) series.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Every load-bearing claim is verified in code. (1) OLD anchor is the TRUE external Gamma createdAt: opening-capture/pure.ts:56-62 computes hoursSinceListing = now − createdAtGamma (doc'd "TRUE Gamma listing time"); handler.ts:257 sets createdAtGamma = ev.createdAt (gamma.ts:96-97 confirms this is the raw Gamma listing time); 0086_google_paper.sql:88-93 gates on opening_captures.hours_since_listing (min<1) and emits s.hours_since_listing / s.created_at_gamma verbatim. (2) NEW anchor is internal ingestion time: 0088:44 gates on min(ms.captured_at − me.first_seen)/3600 < 1, 0088:69 sets createdAtGamma = me.first_seen, 0088:71 sets hoursSinceListing = captured_at − first_seen. (3) me.first_seen is discovery time, NOT Gamma createdAt: upsert_event (0012_discovery_rpcs.sql:117-120) inserts first_seen=now() and the on-conflict branch updates only last_seen, so first_seen is permanently the ingestion timestamp — never Gamma createdAt. (4) Fresh gate is near-tautological: depth_capture_targets (0087:77-106) walks only already-ingested near-dated buckets, freshest-first, on a */5 cron; 0087 header line 7 states 98.9% of listings are snapshotted within 1h of first_seen, so the earliest depth row lands ~one cron cycle after first_seen → min(captured_at−first_seen)<1h holds by construction, so the gate no longer selects the flat-open cohort it used to (which genuinely required opening-capture to have caught the market within 1h of true Gamma listing). (5) The 24h entry-age cap secondary claim holds: google-bucket-replay.ts:135 (maxEntryAgeH:24) and :270-271 reject on age>maxEntryAgeH using hoursSinceListing, and :315 logs entryAgeH from the same field — so a late-discovered, already-converged tick is both admitted as 'fresh' and logged at an understated age. The codebase itself flags this exact anti-pattern: opening-convergence.ts:78 documents the anchor as "now − createdAtGamma at capture (NOT first-sighting — the listing-anchor fix)"; 0088 reintroduces first-sighting. Severity high (kept): it is analytics-only (no capital), but it silently changes the population and the meaning of both the flat-open filter and entry-age over which the headline Google forward-paper §9R-E verdict is computed, and the migration's retained precondition (parity check vs opening_captures) is framed around execAsk/execBid depth, not the listing anchor, so nothing in the pipeline would catch the swap.

confirmed.title: No per-tick time budget on the 800-bucket CLOB walk + terminal-only write → a slow/rate-limited tick can blow the edge wall-clock and drop the whole tick's depth write
confirmed.description: depthCapture walks up to TARGET_LIMIT=800 buckets via mapLimit at WALK_CONCURRENCY=8, each fetch bounded at timeoutMs=6000 with retries:1 (up to ~12s per bucket worst case), and performs the SINGLE record_depth_captures write only AFTER all walks resolve (lines 160-177). Unlike both sibling jobs — opening-capture guards with SEED_TIME_BUDGET_MS=110s, google-paper-panel with FETCH_BUDGET_MS=270s — this job has NO time/wall-clock budget. depth_capture_targets is the broad, non-city-scoped near-dated universe (~45 cities × active near-dated events × ~8 buckets can realistically approach the 800 cap on busy days). The walk runs in EdgeRuntime.waitUntil under the ~400s isolate wall clock; if a large fraction of /book fetches are slow/rate-limited, 100 rounds/worker × up to ~12s exceeds 400s and the isolate is killed BEFORE the terminal write, so zero depth accrues that tick, complete_job_run never fires (the run row lingers 'running' until stale), and market_snapshots.depth silently stops growing — the exact silent-stall failure mode 0087 was built to eliminate. Freshest-first ordering in depth_capture_targets mitigates rate-limit starvation of the flat-open buckets but does not bound total wall time. Fix: add a per-invocation time budget (like opening-capture) and/or flush writes incrementally so a truncated walk still persists partial depth.
confirmed.failureScenario: Busy day: depth_capture_targets returns ~800 near-dated buckets. CLOB is degraded so many /book calls hit the 6s timeout + 1 retry (~12s each). 800/8 = 100 rounds/worker × up to ~12s > the ~400s edge isolate wall clock → EdgeRuntime terminates the isolate before the single record_depth_captures call → 0 depth rows written for the tick, complete_job_run never runs (run stuck 'running'), and the /convergence Google panel's durable depth source silently stops accruing.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Every load-bearing claim verifies against the code. handler.ts:160-177: depthCapture walks up to TARGET_LIMIT=800 buckets via mapLimit at WALK_CONCURRENCY=8, each fetch bounded timeoutMs:6000/retries:1, and performs the SINGLE record_depth_captures write only after mapLimit fully resolves — all-or-nothing, no incremental flush and no wall-clock/Date.now() budget anywhere in the handler (verified absent). packages/io/src/http.ts:32-37 confirms retries:1 = 2 attempts × 6s + one ~0.5s backoff ≈ 12.5s worst case per bucket. The sibling budgets the finding cites are real: opening-capture SEED_TIME_BUDGET_MS=110_000 (handler.ts:44) and google-paper-panel FETCH_BUDGET_MS=270_000 (handler.ts:49); convergence-panel (240s) and maker-exit-panel (270s) add the same guard, each with explicit 'stays under the ~400s isolate wall' arithmetic — depth-capture is the lone book-walking job with no budget. runJob.ts:41-48/95-131 + depth-capture/index.ts confirm the walk runs in EdgeRuntime.waitUntil under the ~400s isolate wall and that complete_job_run fires only after the handler resolves; a killed isolate leaves the run row 'running' (silently reclaimed via claim_job_run stale takeover) and, because the kill is not a thrown error, never hits the notifySlack(JOB_FAIL) path. Migration 0087:75-107 confirms depth_capture_targets is the broad, non-city-scoped near-dated universe capped at 800, and — a smoking gun — line 76 documents an intended 'per-tick budget' that was never implemented (freshest-first ordering was built to pair with a guard that is missing). No deadman watches market_snapshots.depth (capture_deadman_check watches opening_captures, bot_deadman_check watches bot ticks; 0087/0088 register none), so a stall is genuinely silent. Arithmetic holds even at the typical ~315-bucket load: 315/8 ≈ 40 buckets × 12.5s all-hang ≈ 500s > 400s → isolate killed before the terminal write → 0 depth rows that tick; sustained CLOB rate-limiting repeats this, silently stalling the depth column that feeds the repointed (0088) Google panel's execAsk/execBid — the exact silent-stall class 0087 was built to eliminate. Refutation attempts fail: the pg_net 4.5s cron timeout only sees the fast 202 (the walk continues in waitUntil), the write is provably all-or-nothing, and the failure pages nothing. Severity corrected to medium (not higher): it is a tail ops-risk requiring severe/sustained CLOB degradation and partially self-heals via freshest-first re-walk once CLOB recovers, but it is a real, verifiable divergence from the explicitly-documented sibling budget pattern. File paths: supabase/functions/depth-capture/handler.ts, supabase/functions/depth-capture/index.ts, supabase/functions/_shared/runJob.ts, packages/io/src/http.ts, supabase/functions/opening-capture/handler.ts, supabase/functions/google-paper-panel/handler.ts, supabase/migrations/0087_depth_capture.sql.

confirmed.title: depth-capture walks every targeted bucket with no two-sided-quote gate, so the panel can now enter asks-only buckets (no bid → no exit) that the old opening-capture path filtered out
confirmed.description: Old opening-capture only walked/stored depth for TRADEABLE buckets — it pre-filtered `b.bestBid != null && b.bestAsk != null && !(bestBid===0 && bestAsk===1)` (handler.ts:242-244) before walking, so a one-sided (asks-only) bucket got execAsk=null and was NOT enterable by the google engine (fin(ask) false). depth_capture_targets (0087) applies no such filter and walkBucketFull computes execAsk from book.asks[0] even when bestBid is null (execBid then falls back to NaN→null). So the repointed panel now stores a non-null execAsk for asks-only buckets, and replayGoogleBracket will ENTER one whose ask lands in [0.10,0.12] — a bucket with no bid, hence no execBid, hence no TP/SL, held to resolution. This precisely bites at the flat open, where the forecast-center bucket is often quoted asks-only before bids arrive. Net effect: the entry population (and its hold-to-resolution loss profile) differs from the old path.
confirmed.failureScenario: At a fresh flat open the Google-predicted center bucket has asks resting at 0.11 but no bids yet (bestBid null). Old path: bucket not tradeable → execAsk null → event not entered at that tick. New path: walkBucketFull returns execAsk≈0.11, execBid null → entry gate fires → the panel buys and, with execBid perpetually null, holds to resolution, adding a trade the old path never took.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: The parity gap is real and every link verified against the code. OLD path: opening-capture/handler.ts:242-244 pre-filters `tradeable = b.bestBid != null && b.bestAsk != null && !(b.bestBid===0 && b.bestAsk===1)` BEFORE walking, so an asks-only bucket (bestBid null) is never walked; buildOpeningCaptureRow (pure.ts:135) then stores `execAsk: d?.execAsk ?? null` = null for it; 0086 google_paper_inputs reads `b->'execAsk'` = null → replayGoogleBracket's entry gate `fin(ask)` is false → not entered. NEW path: depth_capture_targets (0087:77-107) applies NO two-sided-quote filter; depth-capture/handler.ts:160 walks every target and walkBucketFull (:102-125) derives execAsk from book.asks[0] via executableAsk (edge.ts:26 returns finite cost/filled even with zero bids) → non-null execAsk, while executableBid on empty bids → NaN → execBid null; record_depth_captures stores the non-null execAsk and 0088 caps (:84) surfaces `ms.depth->'execAsk'`. The engine's entry test (google-bucket-replay.ts:261) requires only `fin(ask) && ask>0 && ask∈[askMin,askMax]` with NO execBid check, so an asks-only bucket priced 10-12¢ IS entered; the exit walk (:334-351) skips ticks where execBid is null (`!fin(mark)` → continue), so it never fires TP/SL and settles at resolution (:354-359) — precisely the failure scenario. Neither google-paper-panel/handler.ts nor buildGoogleView re-filters by bid presence. The divergence changes the entry population and the hold-to-resolution loss profile the panel measures, and 0088's own header frames the cutover as requiring a parity check vs opening_captures — which this violates. Severity medium (not higher): this is a DORMANT analytics/paper panel (no capital), 0088 is a staged not-yet-applied cutover, and the impact is a measurement/§9R-E-gate skew rather than a crash or capital loss.

confirmed.title: handler.test.ts only exercises the trivial full-fill book — the job's entire reason for existing (execAsk diverging from best_ask on thin books) plus partial-fill, empty-book, and perPositionUsd wiring are untested
confirmed.description: The only book fixture (DEEP, line 28) has a 2000-share best level that fully fills a $20 buy, so every test asserts execAsk==best_ask (line 79). But the job exists precisely because execAsk DIVERGES from best_ask (+5.85¢ measured) on the thin longshot books the Google panel buys. Missing cases: (a) PARTIAL LADDER — a book too thin to fill perPositionUsd/bestAsk shares at L1, so executableAsk walks into L2+ (execAsk>bestAsk) AND fillableShares<targetShares; the handler (handler.ts:111,125) takes avgPrice whenever it is finite and NEVER checks fillableShares, so a partial fill is silently emitted as if it were a full-position entry price — untested and unverified as intended vs bug; (b) EMPTY/one-sided book (asks:[]) that is fetchable — walkBucketFull returns a row with best_ask=null/execAsk=null/depthUsd=0 that IS written (distinct from the throw→skip path the one test covers); (c) a config row setting a NON-default perPositionUsd that actually changes targetShares and thus which levels get walked (only the default 20 is exercised via getConfigRows:[]); (d) parseBotConfig throwing → default-20 fallback (handler.ts:148-150).
confirmed.failureScenario: A future refactor mis-threads perPositionUsd (e.g. computes targetShares off mid instead of bestAsk) or fails to distinguish a partial from a full fill. Every handler.test case still passes because the DEEP fixture fills any share count at the best level, so the exec-price wiring — the one thing this handler adds over core — ships broken and green.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
All four sub-claims verify against the actual code. The test file (supabase/functions/depth-capture/handler.test.ts) has exactly three `it` blocks, and every one that walks a book uses the single DEEP fixture (line 28): `rawBook([[0.11,2000],[0.12,1000]], [[0.1,2000],[0.09,500]])`. With the default perPositionUsd=20, targetShares = 20/0.11 ≈ 182 shares, which the 2000-share best level fills entirely, so execAsk == best_ask (asserted line 79). The throwToken test (line 85) still returns DEEP for the non-throwing token. So no test ever exercises execAsk diverging from best_ask — which handler.ts's own docstring (lines 5–10) names as the entire reason the job exists ("walks the TRUE CLOB depth ... writes the COMPUTED depth {execAsk...}" for "cheap longshot buckets ... [that] carry only TOP-OF-BOOK").

(a) PARTIAL LADDER — CONFIRMED. handler.ts:111 destructures only `.avgPrice` from `executableAsk(book, targetShares)` and :125 emits it whenever `Number.isFinite(exec)`. executableAsk (edge.ts:12–27) returns `avgPrice = filled>0 ? cost/filled : NaN` and a separate `fillableShares` field whose docstring explicitly states "fillableShares < sizeShares signals insufficient depth" (edge.ts:9); executableBid's docstring (edge.ts:34–37) goes further — "a bracket must require fillableShares ≥ heldShares before honoring a TP/SL mark." The handler never reads fillableShares, so a partial fill's average price is silently emitted as a full-position execAsk. No fixture is thin enough to trigger this, so it is untested and its intended-vs-bug status is unverified.

(b) EMPTY/one-sided fetchable book — CONFIRMED. Trace with asks:[] → bestAsk=null → targetShares=0 (line 110) → exec=NaN → execAsk=null, depthUsd=0, and walkBucketFull RETURNS a row (not null), so it is WRITTEN — a distinct path from the throw→catch→return-null skip (line 133–135) that the "unfetchable book" test covers. No test supplies an empty/one-sided but fetchable book.

(c) NON-default perPositionUsd — CONFIRMED. makeCtx hardwires `getConfigRows: async () => []` (line 37); parseBotConfig([]) falls back to BOT_DEFAULTS.perPositionUsd = 20 (opening-convergence.ts:783/876, OPENING_DEFAULTS:270). No test sets a config row that changes targetShares and thus which levels get walked.

(d) parseBotConfig-throw fallback — CONFIRMED. The catch at handler.ts:148–150 is never reached; getConfigRows returns [] and never throws.

The only other depth-capture test files are the sibling arb-depth-capture handler (a different function) and migrations.test.ts (structural). Severity medium is appropriate: this is a genuine, verifiable test gap on the executable-price wiring that is the sole value this handler adds over core, feeding google_paper_inputs (migration 0088 repoint) — a future refactor mis-threading perPositionUsd or conflating partial vs full fills would ship green. Not downgrading because the untested surface is precisely the job's raison d'être; not upgrading because it is a coverage gap, not a demonstrated live-wrong output.

confirmed.title: No end-to-end test of the record_depth_captures DepthRow ↔ jsonb_to_recordset column contract — a key-name drift silently inserts NULLs or drops every row with no error
confirmed.description: handler.test.ts STUBS record_depth_captures (it only records the args), and migrations.test.ts never executes the real function — the only references to it (lines 368-369) are the migration-filename comment strings. So the contract between the handler's emitted row keys {bucket_id,best_bid,best_ask,mid,spread,depth} (handler.ts DepthRow, lines 53-67) and the SQL recordset columns `r(bucket_id uuid, best_bid numeric, ..., depth jsonb)` (0087:57) is verified NOWHERE. jsonb_to_recordset matches by key NAME and silently yields NULL for any missing/renamed key; combined with `where r.bucket_id is not null` (0087:58), a drift on bucket_id would drop 100% of rows and return 0 with no exception. This is the data foundation of the entire repoint, and there is no PGlite round-trip asserting a handler-shaped row lands in market_snapshots with depth intact and readable by google_paper_inputs.
confirmed.failureScenario: Someone renames DepthRow.best_bid to bestBid (camelCase, matching the rest of the codebase's convention). Types still compile, handler.test still passes (it never runs SQL). In prod every depth row inserts best_bid=NULL (or, if bucket_id drifts, inserts nothing); the repointed panel reads null/absent depth and silently degrades, with no failing test and no job error.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: The test-gap is real and every factual claim verifies. (1) depth-capture/handler.test.ts:40-43 STUBS record_depth_captures — it intercepts the RPC name, stores the args, and returns a synthetic [{record_depth_captures: p_rows.length}]; the real SQL never executes. (2) A grep of all *.test.ts finds record_depth_captures only at migrations.test.ts:368-369,371,988, all inside comment/cron-comment strings — there is no `select public.record_depth_captures(...)` call anywhere in the suite. (3) The handler emits DepthRow with keys {bucket_id,best_bid,best_ask,mid,spread,depth} (handler.ts:53-67). (4) The SQL recordset is `r(bucket_id uuid, best_bid numeric, best_ask numeric, mid numeric, spread numeric, depth jsonb)` (0087:56-57) with `where r.bucket_id is not null` (0087:58) and `get diagnostics v_n = row_count` (0087:65). jsonb_to_recordset matches by key NAME, so a renamed/missing key silently yields NULL; a bucket_id drift NULLs the filter key, drops 100% of rows, and returns 0 with no exception — and the handler never asserts inserted==walked (handler.ts:173 just logs), so no job error. (5) The repoint reads exactly these back: google_paper_inputs consumes ms.depth->'execAsk'/'execBid'/'depthUsd' filtered on `where ms.depth is not null` (0088:38,84-95), so the untested write contract is the panel's exec-price data foundation. The drift is invisible to typecheck (SQL column names are untyped string literals vs the TS interface) and to both existing test layers. This is precisely the silent-shape class the codebase has repeatedly shipped green and now guards elsewhere (the 0044/0081 port-shape bugfix migrations and the dedicated "port invariant tripwire" suite at migrations.test.ts:1046), which makes the absence of a PGlite round-trip guard here an in-character, legitimate gap. Severity held at medium rather than higher because the code is currently correct (keys match today), the surface is an analytics-only/rail-DORMANT panel with no capital at risk, and the staged cutover has an explicit one-time manual parity-verification step at 0088 apply time that would catch a fully-NULL depth column — though post-cutover handler edits would not be caught by that manual gate, so the guard is genuinely warranted.

confirmed.title: Silent truncation past p_limit=800 is unlogged, and depth-capture's unconditional every-5-min write adds ~200k rows/day to market_snapshots on a Micro instance that already saturated
confirmed.description: depth_capture_targets caps at LIMIT 800 (0087:106) ordered by first_seen DESC. The near-dated live universe realistically approaches/exceeds that: ~2-3 live target_dates × 45 cities × ~7-9 buckets ≈ 700-1200 buckets. When it exceeds 800, the DESC ordering silently drops the OLDEST-first_seen (closest-to-resolution) buckets — exactly the ones whose TP/SL/hold-to-resolution trajectory the panel needs — and NOTHING logs it: the handler records stats.targets = targets.length (handler.ts:181), i.e. the already-capped count, so targets.length===800 is indistinguishable from 'exactly 800 exist' and the operator gets no signal that buckets were dropped. Separately, depth-capture walks unconditionally (no delta gate) and writes ~1 row/bucket/tick → up to ~800×288 ≈ 230k market_snapshots rows/day ON TOP of poll-markets, from a SECOND */5 external-fetch walker (up to 800 CLOB /book fetches at concurrency 8, 6s+1retry each). The handoff acknowledges the saturation risk (07-06/07 Micro saturated at opening-capture */2) but mitigates only reactively ('back off if latency climbs') and never quantifies this added unconditional write/fetch load.
confirmed.failureScenario: On a busy day 900 near-dated buckets qualify. depth_capture_targets returns the 800 freshest by first_seen; the 100 oldest (maturing toward resolution) get no depth ticks, so the panel's exit/resolution replay for those events silently loses coverage. stats.targets logs 800 with no 'cap hit' warning, so the gap is invisible; meanwhile the table gains ~230k depth rows/day and the second */5 fetch burst re-creates the saturation condition on Micro.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Both halves of this compound ops-risk finding are grounded in the actual code. (1) Silent truncation: depth_capture_targets caps at `limit greatest(p_limit,1)` with p_limit default 800 (0087_depth_capture.sql:79,106) ordered `me.first_seen desc nulls last` (0087:105) — the migration's own comment (0087:76) confirms this deliberately prioritizes the freshest/flat-open events, so once >800 buckets qualify the DESC order drops the oldest-first_seen (maturing/near-resolution) buckets. The handler logs only `targets: targets.length` (handler.ts:181), which is the already-capped RPC result; no un-capped count is fetched and there is no cap-hit warning anywhere, so targets.length===800 is indistinguishable from 'exactly 800 exist' — total observability gap, confirmed. The trigger is near-term realistic, not hypothetical: the handoff (DEPTH-CAPTURE-REPOINT-HANDOFF.md:40) reports the current live universe is already '~73 events / 45 cities' → ~500-650 buckets at 7-9 buckets/event, far above the migration comment's '315 typical' (0087:32) and close to the 800 cap; a busier multi-date day exceeds it, and those dropped buckets never get depth ticks that day. (2) Unconditional load: mapLimit walks every target and record_depth_captures writes every walked row every */5 tick with no delta gate (handler.ts:160-177; cron */5 at 0087:133); up to 800 CLOB /book fetches at concurrency 8, 6s+1 retry (handler.ts:33,97-100). Row math ~230k/day at the 800 ceiling ('up to', accurate) / ~144k-187k/day at the current ~500-650 buckets × 288 ticks, on top of poll-markets' own upsert_market_snapshots writes (poll-markets/handler.ts:246). The Micro saturation is documented (CLAUDE.md 07-06/07) and the handoff mitigates only reactively — 'if per-tick latency climbs, back off depth-capture' (DEPTH-CAPTURE-REPOINT-HANDOFF.md:71-73) — never quantifying the added write/fetch load, exactly as the finding states. Severity held at medium rather than raised or dropped: the >800 truncation is conditional (though the live ~500-650 makes it a realistic near-term ceiling) and the consuming panel is DORMANT/paper, so the concrete impact is degraded analytics-coverage of the resolution tail plus a real second */5 external-fetch/write walker on infra that saturated two days prior — a legitimate tests-and-ops observability + scaling gap, not a capital-at-risk correctness bug.

confirmed.title: hoursSinceListing re-anchored to market_events.first_seen (ingestion time) instead of the Gamma createdAt listing time, shifting the fresh-universe and maxEntryAgeH gates
confirmed.description: first_seen is guaranteed non-null in `caps` (the `fresh` CTE requires `me.first_seen is not null` at line 41 and caps only includes fresh events), so hoursSinceListing cannot be null and won't crash the TS `fin()` gate — that part is safe. But the ANCHOR changed: original hours_since_listing was measured from the TRUE Gamma listing time (opening-capture/pure.ts:56-59 uses ev.createdAt/createdAtGamma), while 0088 measures from me.first_seen (our ingestion first-seen; the migration itself calls it 'the listing proxy'). This drives BOTH (a) the fresh filter `having min(...) < 1` and (b) replayGoogleBracket's maxEntryAgeH=24h gate. Because first_seen >= the true Gamma createdAt (we cannot snapshot before the market exists), every event's reconstructed hoursSinceListing is <= the original, so the 24h age gate is systematically looser (admits entries 0086 would reject as >24h-old). Separately, depth rows only begin accruing once a market is near-dated (depth_capture_targets walks target_date <= now+3d), so a market listed >~3 days before target_date has its first depth row land >1h after first_seen, giving min hoursSinceListing > 1 and EXCLUDING it from `fresh`, whereas the opening_captures path (captured near true listing) included it. Net: the fresh universe and the entered population diverge from the baseline. Impact is bounded by ingestion lead-time (small for markets listed ~1-2 days ahead) and is documented as intentional, hence low severity — but it is still a measurable parity divergence the reviewer flagged.
confirmed.failureScenario: A daily-high market for target_date D listed 5 days early (Gamma createdAt = D-5). depth-capture first walks it at ~D-3 (target_date enters the now+3d window), so the earliest depth row's captured_at - first_seen ≈ 48h → min hoursSinceListing = 48 > 1 → event dropped from `fresh` and never appears in the Google panel, even though 0086 (opening_captures captured near D-5 listing, min ≈ 0) treated it as fresh and scored it. Conversely, for a market whose first_seen lags its true Gamma createdAt, a tick that is 30h-since-true-listing reads as, say, 22h-since-first_seen and passes the 24h maxEntryAgeH gate that the original would have failed.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
The parity divergence is real and directly visible in code. Baseline 0086 (0086_google_paper.sql:111,113) returns hoursSinceListing/createdAtGamma from opening_captures, whose hours_since_listing is computed in opening-capture/pure.ts (hoursSinceListing at :56-62 → buildOpeningCaptureRow :148,:173) against the TRUE Gamma listing time (ev.createdAt → createdAtGamma). 0088 re-anchors both: line 71 computes hoursSinceListing = extract(epoch from (ms.captured_at - me.first_seen))/3600 and line 69 sets createdAtGamma = me.first_seen — the migration's own comments (:10-11, :30-31) call first_seen "the listing proxy," i.e. explicitly NOT the true listing anchor.

This anchor feeds BOTH gates the finding names: (a) the fresh filter `having min(... ms.captured_at - me.first_seen ...) < 1` (0088:44), and (b) the maxEntryAgeH=24h gate — GOOGLE_DEFAULTS.maxEntryAgeH=24 (google-bucket-replay.ts:135), enforced at :269-274 against ticks[i].hoursSinceListing, which flows RPC → RawCaptureRow.hoursSinceListing → buildEvents ReplayTick.hoursSinceListing (opening-bracket-ingest.ts:119) → the replay's age gate. Since first_seen >= true Gamma createdAt (we cannot snapshot before a market exists), reconstructed ages are systematically <= the originals, so the 24h age gate is directionally looser (Prong A).

Prong B is also confirmed: depth_capture_targets (0087:102-104) walks ms.depth only for target_date between now-1d and now+(p_max_lead+1) (default p_max_lead=2 → now+3d). For a market first_seen near listing (0087:8: ~98.9% snapshotted within 1h of first_seen) but listed >3 days before target_date, the earliest depth row lands >>1h after first_seen → min hoursSinceListing > 1 → dropped from `fresh`, whereas the opening_captures path captured it near true listing (min≈0) and kept it. So the fresh universe and entered population genuinely diverge from the 0086 baseline for early-listed markets.

The crash angle is correctly conceded as safe: fresh requires me.first_seen is not null (0088:41) and caps only joins fresh events, so hoursSinceListing is never null in the payload. This is analytics-only on a DORMANT rail and the migration explicitly documents the proxy and demands a manual parity check before cutover ("apply ONLY after ... a parity check vs the (revived) opening_captures path looks sane"), so low severity is accurate — it is a genuine, bounded, intentional-but-measurable parity shift, exactly as flagged.

confirmed.title: depth_capture_targets silently truncates at 800 buckets with no saturation signal
confirmed.description: The near-dated window spans 5 target_dates (today-1 .. today + p_max_lead + 1 = today+3) across the ~45-city capture universe. When the live 'highest' universe exceeds 800 buckets, `limit greatest(p_limit,1)` drops the trailing rows with no raise/alarm — the only observable symptom is the handler's `targets` stat pinning at 800. The `order by me.first_seen desc` prioritization means the OLDEST (still-resolving / near-resolution) events' buckets are the ones dropped, which is the least-bad set for the entry strategy; but because the ORDER BY is deterministic, the SAME trailing buckets are dropped on every tick until the universe shrinks, so a starved event's depth is never captured. The handler comment (~315 typical) assumes ~45 concurrent events, but 3-4 simultaneously-open target_dates across most cities is enough to blow past 800.
confirmed.failureScenario: On a day where 'highest' markets for 4 dates (yesterday-unresolved + today + tomorrow + day+2) are simultaneously open across ~45 cities (~135 events x ~7 buckets = ~945 buckets), depth_capture_targets returns exactly 800; ~145 trailing (oldest-first_seen) buckets are never walked, so market_snapshots.depth stays null for them and the repointed google_paper_inputs (0088) silently under-covers those events' resolution-time ticks — with no operator-visible warning.
confirmed.verifyReasoning:
Every code-level mechanism the finding describes is present exactly as claimed in `supabase/migrations/0087_depth_capture.sql`:

1. Silent truncation (line 106): `limit greatest(p_limit, 1)`. The handler (`supabase/functions/depth-capture/handler.ts` line 155) calls it with `p_limit: TARGET_LIMIT` where `TARGET_LIMIT = 800` (line 32). Grepping the whole `depth-capture/` dir, `800` appears ONLY as that constant — there is no `if (targets.length >= TARGET_LIMIT)` check, no raise, no warning. The stats object (lines 179-188) emits `targets: targets.length` and nothing else, so on saturation the sole observable symptom is `targets` pinning at exactly 800, precisely as the finding states.

2. Oldest-first drop (line 105): `order by me.first_seen desc nulls last, me.id, mb.bucket_idx`. `first_seen desc` puts newest events first; `limit` keeps the head, so the OLDEST (near-resolution) events' buckets fall off the tail. The tiebreak (`me.id`, `bucket_idx`) is fully deterministic, so the SAME trailing buckets are dropped every tick until the universe composition changes — matching the "starved event's depth is never captured" claim.

3. Downstream impact is real: 0088 (`google_paper_inputs`) pulls `caps` only `where ms.depth is not null` (line 95) for `fresh` events selected by `min hoursSinceListing < 1` (line 44). A fresh event is walked at listing (top of the order) but can drift below the cap as it ages toward resolution and the universe grows — so its exit-leg (execBid TP/SL) resolution-time ticks would silently stay depth=null and be excluded. Confirmed mechanism.

The 5-date near-dated window (line 103-104: today-1 .. today + max_lead + 1 = today+3) is also as described.

Severity stays LOW (as claimed) because the trigger is latent, not active: `docs/ops/DEPTH-CAPTURE-REPOINT-HANDOFF.md` line 39 records the measured universe as ~73 events / 45 cities, and the handler comment's own ~7 buckets/event gives ≈511 buckets — ~64% of the 800 cap, ~1.6x headroom. The finding's ~135-event/945-bucket saturation scenario requires roughly doubling concurrent open dates/city (plausible on a lagged-grading day but not currently occurring), and when it does fire it drops the least-relevant (near-resolution) buckets — a point the finding itself concedes. It also feeds a DORMANT/CLOSED analytics paper panel, not live capital. So this is a genuine missing-guardrail ops-risk (silent, deterministic, unsignalled truncation) that the code truly exhibits, correctly rated low.

confirmed.title: depth-capture injects book_top3-null rows into shared market_snapshots, shadowing 'latest snapshot' reads (contra 'only ADDS depth')
confirmed.description: record_depth_captures INSERTs entirely NEW market_snapshots rows (fresh captured_at, book_top3 null, last_trade null) every 5 min for near-dated live buckets — it does not merely 'ADD depth' to existing rows as the header comment (l.24-25, l.44-45) frames it. Any existing consumer that reads the LATEST snapshot per bucket via `order by captured_at desc limit 1` can now return a depth-capture row instead of a poll-markets row. dash event-detail (0022 l.81-85) exposes `lastSnapshot.bookTop3` exactly this way. poll-markets writes snapshots on a delta/heartbeat decision (comment in upsert_market_snapshots, 0018 l.83-86), so for a flat/stable near-dated bucket a depth-capture row is frequently the newest. Money path is unaffected (recommendations compute edges in-tick; get_known_events/amsterdam/city sims read mid/best_ask, which depth rows do populate) — impact is confined to latest-snapshot book_top3 display.
confirmed.failureScenario: Operator opens a near-dated live event in the dashboard between poll ticks, where depth-capture wrote the most-recent snapshot; the ladder's `lastSnapshot.bookTop3` renders null (EdgeChart shows 'book truncated') for those buckets even though poll had walked a real book, because the latest market_snapshots row for the bucket is a depth-capture row that never carries book_top3.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: The defect is real and reproducible from the code. record_depth_captures (0087 l.54–55) INSERTs entirely new market_snapshots rows: column list is (bucket_id, best_bid, best_ask, mid, spread, last_trade, depth, captured_at), with last_trade selected as null and captured_at = p_captured_at (a fresh tick instant). book_top3 is NOT in the column list, so every inserted row has book_top3 = NULL (0004 l.77 default). The depth-capture handler (handler.ts l.141 capturedAt = now.toISOString(); l.155/160–173) walks EVERY near-dated live 'highest' bucket — depth_capture_targets (0087 l.93) joins all market_buckets of the event, not just edge candidates — and writes one such row per bucket every 5 min (0087 l.133 '*/5'). dash_event_detail (0022 l.81–86) reads each ladder bucket's lastSnapshot.bookTop3 = ms.book_top3 via `where ms.bucket_id = b.id order by ms.captured_at desc limit 1`, exactly the latest-snapshot read the finding names. poll-markets writes snapshots on a delta/heartbeat gate (handler.ts l.234–241 `if (moved || lastAge >= heartbeatMs)`) and only attaches book_top3 to its OWN freshly-inserted latest row for the ≤15 edge candidates (l.353 attach_book_to_snapshot; 0018 l.134–136 targets the captured_at desc limit 1 row). Therefore, between poll ticks the 5-min depth-capture rows are newer and become the latest row per bucket, so dash_event_detail returns bookTop3: null for near-dated live buckets whose real poll-walked book lives on an older row. The header comment (l.24–25/44–45: 'only ADDS depth', 'coexists') is functionally misleading for latest-snapshot reads. One minor wording imprecision that does not refute: a fully null bookTop3 makes edge-display.ts toBook() return null (l.72–73) → recomputeEdgeRows yields execAsk===null → EdgeChart renders the reasons/'no_book' path (EdgeChart l.96), not the literal 'book truncated' string (l.99, which fires on !comparable). Different label, identical operator-visible effect (ladder shows no usable book for buckets that had a real walked one). Money path is genuinely unaffected (recommendations fetch books in-tick; sims/get_known_events read mid/best_ask, which depth rows populate), so the claimed 'low' severity — display/analytics-only — is correct.

confirmed.title: depth-capture walks execAsk/execBid at botCfg.perPositionUsd while the Google panel replays at hardcoded GOOGLE_DEFAULTS.perPositionUsd — an un-enforced size invariant (currently dormant at 20, pre-existing)
confirmed.description: depthCapture sources the walk size from parseBotConfig(getConfigRows()).perPositionUsd (default 20, clamp allows 0..1e7) and prices execAsk = executableAsk(book, perPositionUsd/bestAsk) / execBid accordingly (lines 144-147, 110-114). The consumer, google-paper-panel, replays entries via googleCfg → GOOGLE_DEFAULTS.perPositionUsd = 20 (google-bucket-replay.ts:124-141) and does NOT read botCfg for the replay stake. The two coincide ONLY while config key bot.perPositionUsd stays at its default 20; nothing enforces that. If the operator sets bot.perPositionUsd for the opening-convergence bot to any other value, market_snapshots.depth will carry execAsk/execBid walked at that size while the panel prices fills as if buying $20 of depth, biasing the entry/TP fills the repointed panel reads. NOTE: this exact coupling pre-existed in the 0086 path (opening-capture also walked at botCfg.perPositionUsd while the panel replayed at 20), so the repoint PRESERVES parity rather than breaking it, and it is inactive today (both are 20). Flagged per the explicit scrutiny ask; the durable fix is to source the walk size from GOOGLE_DEFAULTS.perPositionUsd (the size the panel actually replays at) rather than the bot's stake, or assert the two are equal.
confirmed.failureScenario: Operator sets config bot.perPositionUsd = 150 for the opening-convergence bot. depth-capture then walks and stores execAsk/execBid for $150 of book depth; google-paper-panel replays entries at $20 (GOOGLE_DEFAULTS), so the panel reads exec prices computed at a 7.5× different size than it claims to trade — silently distorting the Google-panel entry/TP economics. (Benign while bot.perPositionUsd == 20.)
confirmed.verifyReasoning: The un-enforced size invariant is real and present in the repo. depth-capture/handler.ts:144-147 sources the book-walk size from parseBotConfig(getConfigRows()).perPositionUsd; opening-convergence.ts:876 shows that key is clamp('bot.perPositionUsd', 20, 0, 1e7) — default 20 but operator-settable up to 1e7. Lines 110-114 and 125-126 compute execAsk/execBid by walking the book for that perPositionUsd of shares and store them into market_snapshots.depth. The repoint migration 0088_google_paper_repoint.sql:84-85 makes google_paper_inputs read ms.depth->'execAsk'/'execBid' from exactly that column. The consumer chain google-paper-panel/handler.ts:94,147 → google-bucket-view.ts:296 (spreads {...cfg}, only overrides tpAbs/slAbs) → google-bucket-replay.ts fills entry at the stored execAsk (line 261/309), exits on the stored execBid (line 335), and sizes shares at cfg.perPositionUsd = GOOGLE_DEFAULTS.perPositionUsd = 20 (lines 124-141, 303) — never reading bot config for the stake. Nothing asserts botCfg.perPositionUsd == 20; the depth-capture comment at line 143 even mis-claims they are 'the same per-position stake the panel replays on.' So if the operator sets bot.perPositionUsd (e.g. 150), market_snapshots.depth carries execAsk/execBid walked at $150 of book depth while the panel prices $20 fills — a pessimistic/optimistic distortion of the entry and TP legs the repointed panel reads. Severity is correctly low: both values default to 20 today (benign/dormant), and the Google panel is read-only DORMANT-rail analytics with no capital at risk — worst case is distorted analytics numbers, not a money bug — and it requires the operator to change a live config key. The finding is also honest that the repoint preserves, not introduces, the coupling (the prior 0086 path read opening_captures walked the same way). CONFIRMED as a genuine latent parity defect at low severity.

confirmed.title: Partial per-tick ladder (best-effort walk failure or the 800-target cap) can omit the Google-predicted bucket from the ladder tick, silently dropping the event
confirmed.description: Old opening_captures stored the COMPLETE ladder every tick (all ev.buckets, execAsk=null for un-walked). 0088 builds buckets[] via jsonb_agg over only the market_snapshots depth rows that exist for that (event, tick) — a bucket whose CLOB /book fetch threw (walkBucketFull returns null, best-effort skip) or that was cut by depth_capture_targets' `limit 800` is absent from that tick. buildGoogleView uses the FIRST populated tick as the ladder for googleBucketIdx; winningBucket keys off each present label's own range, so a gap does NOT mis-bucket or crash — it fails closed: if the winning bucket is the missing one, winningBucket throws LadderGapError → googleBucketIdx returns null → the event is dropped (not counted in nGoogleEvents, never entered). This is a non-deterministic sampling reduction vs the old complete-ladder path (target count can approach/exceed 800: up to ~45 cities × several near-dated target_dates × ~7-11 buckets).
confirmed.failureScenario: depth-capture's first tick for an event hits a transient timeout on exactly the bucket Google points at; that tick's jsonb_agg ladder lacks it → googleBucketIdx null → the event is excluded from the panel entirely, even though later ticks carry that bucket with a cheap in-band ask that the old path would have entered.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: The finding's full mechanism is verified in code. NEW path 0088 (lines 80-96) builds each tick's buckets[] via jsonb_agg over `market_snapshots ms join market_buckets mb WHERE ms.depth is not null` grouped by (me.id, ms.captured_at) — so a bucket with no depth row for that captured_at is absent from that tick. Such absence is real and per-bucket: depth-capture/handler.ts walkBucketFull returns null on any /book fetch throw (lines 133-135) and line 164 filters nulls out of the written rows (best-effort, non-atomic per event), and 0087's depth_capture_targets caps at `limit greatest(p_limit,1)` with TARGET_LIMIT=800 (handler.ts line 32; 0087 lines 79/106), ordered first_seen desc/me.id/bucket_idx so overflow cuts an event's tail buckets. The OLD path stored the COMPLETE ladder every tick: opening-capture/pure.ts buildOpeningCaptureRow (lines 126-146) maps over the full args.ev.buckets, setting execAsk=null for un-walked buckets but keeping every bucket present — exactly the parity baseline the finding cites. buildEvents (opening-bracket-ingest.ts lines 113-115) does NOT merge ladders across ticks — each tick's buckets are exactly that RPC row's buckets. buildGoogleView (google-bucket-view.ts line 287) takes the ladder from the FIRST populated tick only, then line 288-289 `predIdx = googleBucketIdx(ladder,...); if (predIdx == null) continue;` drops the event (never counted in nGoogleEvents, never entered). googleBucketIdx (google-bucket-replay.ts lines 179-184) wraps winningBucket in try/catch → null on LadderGapError; winningBucket (buckets.ts lines 129-140) matches each bucket by its own integer [low,high], so a removed interior single-degree °C bucket produces a genuine gap that no neighbor claims → throws → null (fails closed, no mis-bucket, no crash — as the finding states). °F markets are pre-filtered (view line 280) so only °C single-degree ladders are affected, which is where the gap bites hardest. Net: whenever the first populated tick happens to lack exactly the Google-predicted bucket, the new path drops the event pre-replay, whereas the old complete-ladder path would resolve predIdx and let replayGoogleBracket enter on a later in-band cheap tick — a non-deterministic sampling reduction, exactly as claimed. Severity stays low: google_paper_panel is a DORMANT analytics-only forward-paper panel (no capital at risk, all 12 signals falsified), the failure fails closed (silent sample shrinkage, not a wrong figure or crash), and per-bucket fetch failures / the 800 cap are individually rare — though it does mildly undercut the migration's stated 'same shape buildGoogleView consumes' parity intent and the §9R-E sample-size gate.

confirmed.title: Staged cutover relies solely on operator discipline — 0088 is a committed migration, so any future `supabase db push` applies the repoint prematurely; the only guard is a prose caveat
confirmed.description: The whole design depends on applying 0088 (the source cutover) ONLY after depth has accrued and parity is verified. But 0088_google_paper_repoint.sql is a committed, numbered migration in the same directory as everything else, and 0087 is already recorded as applied. Supabase's `db push` diffs local migration files against the applied set and pushes anything pending — so the NEXT `db push` for ANY unrelated later migration (0089+) will sweep 0088 in and cut the panel over to market_snapshots.depth automatically. If that happens before depth has accrued, google_paper_inputs' fresh CTE (0088:32-44, `ms.depth is not null`) matches nothing → nFreshEvents≈0 → the panel silently swaps source and reads empty, and the gate flips to INSUFFICIENT with no indication the source changed. The only mitigation is the handoff's prose caveat (lines 40-42, 'do NOT rely on db push'); there is no technical guard (e.g. a `.staged` suffix, a guard clause requiring depth-row count > N, or holding 0088 out of the migrations dir until cutover). For a change explicitly designed as a reversible staged cutover, a doc note is an insufficient control.
confirmed.failureScenario: Two weeks later an unrelated 0089 migration is deployed via `supabase db push`. db push sees 0088 as pending and applies it too, cutting the Google panel onto market_snapshots.depth before parity was checked. The operator, expecting only 0089, doesn't notice the panel's data source silently changed and its history reset; the gate reads INSUFFICIENT and the cause is invisible.
confirmed.verifyReasoning: Every technical assertion checks out against the actual files. (1) 0088_google_paper_repoint.sql is a committed, normally-named migration in supabase/migrations/ alongside 0085-0087 (confirmed via ls), and it is an unconditional `create or replace function` (0088:14) with NO guard clause conditioning the cutover on depth existing. (2) 0087 is recorded as applied (handoff line 38: "0087 is APPLIED (2026-07-08, via MCP)"). (3) The `db push` mechanism claim is accurate for Supabase — it applies every local migration not yet in remote history, and 0088 sorts before any future 0089, so a future blanket push for unrelated work would sweep 0088 in. Nothing excludes the file. (4) The empty-read failure is real: the rewritten fresh CTE gates on `ms.depth is not null` (0088:38) and the entire capture series is sourced from depth rows (0088:32-44, 90-96); with no accrued depth, fresh→∅ → caps/res/google all empty → panel reads empty → gate INSUFFICIENT, silently, with no signal that the source changed. (5) The only mitigation is genuinely prose: handoff lines 40-42 ("⚠ db push caveat … do NOT rely on db push"); there is no technical control (no .staged suffix, no depth-row-count guard, no exclusion from the dir). So the finding's core assertion — a staged cutover relying solely on operator discipline + a doc note — is exactly what the code shows. Severity corrected medium→low: the blast radius is an analytics-only forward panel (handoff line 83 — poll-markets/money engine/trading rail explicitly NOT changed, rail DORMANT; no capital path), it is fully reversible (rollback documented lines 76-79 = re-apply 0086's body), the panel already reads INSUFFICIENT so no live signal is lost, and the project's shown workflow applies migrations via targeted MCP apply_migration (line 38) rather than blanket db push, making the trigger less likely. Real and worth a cheap technical guard, but the consequence is modest and recoverable, and the author already flagged it — medium overstates it.
